what_this_is: One list of medicines for each condition a criterion depends on, shared by every criterion that needs that condition. A condition is rarely written in a dispensing history; when a medicine that points to it is supplied, the LANTERN asks the pharmacist to confirm the condition. A medicine never proves a condition: the pharmacist decides. NAMES: every ingredient and brand is one the SNOMED CT-AU medicines list (release of 31 October 2026) holds, checked by program; a name it does not hold is not written. LINKS: the link from a medicine to a condition is its Australian registered indication or PBS restriction; each medicine carries the page. A draft until the clinical reviewer says it is right.
reading_stage: Version of 21 November 2026, 03:12. 201 conditions; 1006 medicines that point to a condition: 999 cite a PBS page, a TGA page or the Australian product information, 7 were named by the clinical reviewer, and 0 are marked STILL TO BE CONFIRMED on their list. After the second reading of tonight's new lists: warfarin, dabigatran and enoxaparin point to a history of a blood clot (PINCER-4 concerns a woman on a combined hormonal contraceptive); six medicines that cannot be told apart by ingredient and form moved to the medicines also used.

in_play_note: A criterion named under in_play flags a medicine: a condition question from these lists is asked for it only when a medicine of the named groups of that criterion is supplied (all of the groups when all_of is true, any one of them otherwise). A criterion not named here is asked as soon as a medicine that points to its condition is supplied. Read once from each criterion's own rule by GPT-6.2 Astra on 20 November 2026 (the criteria outside STOPP and START) and on 21 November (the STOPP criteria: the groups of which a supply is required, not a group that only holds a comparison treatment or a medicine that clears the finding). A STOPP criterion not named here is in play when a medicine of any of its own groups is supplied; a START criterion is an omission.
